findings.claim: LoggerMiddleware no longer builds pluginId, endpoint, uname, dsName, dsUID and traceID on the 'Plugin Request Completed' (grafana-data-egress) log line. It now gets them only through m.logger.FromContext(ctx) at line 58. So it silently depends on two things: ContextualLoggerMiddleware sitting above it in CreateMiddlewares, and the tracing traceID log provider being registered globally. Nothing documents or tests that dependency. Neither the new ContextualLoggerMiddleware (contextual_logger_middleware.go:1-69) nor LoggerMiddleware's output has a test. If the chain is reordered, or the contextual middleware is dropped, the fields vanish with no failure. Key order on the line also changes: context fields now come before status/duration.
findings.evidence: All three seats reasoned this from the code; none ran a failing command. No logger_middleware_test.go or contextual_logger_middleware_test.go exists in clientmiddleware/. metrics_middleware_test.go never asserted context or log attributes, at base or now. CreateMiddlewares (pluginsintegration.go:156-187) is the only place that wires the chain, and its current order is correct: Tracing -> Metrics -> ContextualLogger -> Logger, because decorator.go:106 reverses the list. The old 'should live at the top of the middleware stack' comment was deleted from metrics_middleware.go and nothing replaced it. Production output is correct today: the attributes come via log.WithContextualAttributes, and traceID comes from the provider at pkg/infra/tracing/tracing.go:91. A test using the fake would not help, because TestLogger.FromContext returns a fresh logger (fake.go:46). mattpocock ties the gap to contribute/backend/style-guide.md:28 ('covered by unit tests').
findings.reason: Accepted. Three seats agree, and the repo's style guide requires unit coverage. Severity normalised to Minor. Both correctness seats rated it Minor after confirming production behaviour is correct today. Only the advisory mattpocock seat rated it Important, citing the style guide; advisory severity does not block. It is a missing guard, not wrong output. Fix by adding a contract test that runs the CreateMiddlewares stack and asserts pluginId/endpoint/uname/dsName/dsUID/traceID on the egress log line. Also add an ordering note on NewLoggerMiddleware or ContextualLoggerMiddleware. The test depends on the fake.go:46 fix, or on a recording logger.

findings.claim: TestLogger.FromContext returns a new, empty NewTestLogger() instead of f. LoggerMiddleware now logs only through FromContext. So a test that injects a TestLogger always sees InfoLogs.Calls == 0, and the fake cannot be used to test the middleware.
findings.evidence: The code reads 'return NewTestLogger()'. The only production caller is logger_middleware.go:58, which logs only through FromContext. Grep finds no current test that wires a TestLogger into LoggerMiddleware, so nothing fails today; the claim is reasoned. The fake mirrors existing TestLogger.New behaviour (superpowers). mattpocock cites the same behaviour as evidence for the coverage gap.
findings.reason: Accepted. Returning f is a one-line change, it keeps logs observable, and the main-list coverage fix needs it. Not a regression of current tests.

findings.claim: In grafanaInfraLogWrapper.FromContext, the '!ok' fallback (return d.New()) can never run, because the *log.ConcreteLogger type assertion always succeeds. If it ever did run, it would silently drop the context fields.
findings.evidence: ConcreteLogger.FromContext (pkg/infra/log/log.go:203-217) only returns cl or cl.New(...), and both are *ConcreteLogger. mattpocock and open-code-review independently confirmed the branch is unreachable, but listed that as a check rather than a finding. ponytail suggests the simplification: return &grafanaInfraLogWrapper{l: d.l.FromContext(ctx).(*log.ConcreteLogger)}.
findings.reason: Appendix: only two seats raised it. Not fixed. Harmless dead code; leave a 'ponytail:' comment if revisited.
